rules.statement: Mutations that induce a shift in the reading frame are associated with Duchenne muscular dystrophy rather than Becker muscular dystrophy.
rules.exceptions: The reading-frame rule has exceptions; 91% of over 4700 mutations were in agreement, and it held true for 96% of DMD patients and 93% of BMD patients.

sources.quote: In Duchenne patients, mutations induce a shift in the reading frame leading to prematurely truncated, dysfunctional dystrophins.
The reading frame rule holds true for 96% of the DMD patients and 93% of the BMD patients.
Currently, over 4700 mutations have been reported in the Leiden DMD mutation database, of which 91% are in agreement with this rule.

items.item: Condition: the rule is about DMD frameshift variants.
items.reason: Quotes state the reading frame rule applies to DMD patients and that frameshift mutations occur in Duchenne patients.

items.item: Conclusion: such variants point to Duchenne muscular dystrophy rather than Becker muscular dystrophy.
items.reason: Quotes link frameshift to Duchenne patients but never explicitly state these variants point to DMD rather than Becker; BMD is mentioned only as a percentage.

items.item: Scope: this is stated as a general association for such DMD variants, not only for a single reported patient or family, and not only as a difference in frequency between patient groups.
items.reason: Quotes present the association as frequency percentages (96% DMD, 93% BMD), i.e., a frequency difference, not as a general rule beyond frequency.

rules.statement: In-frame mutations are associated with Becker muscular dystrophy rather than Duchenne muscular dystrophy.
rules.exceptions: The reading-frame rule has exceptions; 91% of over 4700 mutations were in agreement, and it held true for 96% of DMD patients and 93% of BMD patients.

sources.quote: In Duchenne patients, mutations induce a shift in the reading frame leading to prematurely truncated, dysfunctional dystrophins. In Becker patients, in-frame mutations allow the synthesis of internally deleted, but largely functional dystrophins.
The reading frame rule holds true for 96% of the DMD patients and 93% of the BMD patients.
Currently, over 4700 mutations have been reported in the Leiden DMD mutation database, of which 91% are in agreement with this rule.

items.item: Condition: the rule is about DMD in-frame deletion or in-frame insertion or in-frame insertion-deletion variants.
items.reason: The quotes state the reading-frame rule for in-frame mutations in DMD/Duchenne and Becker patients, covering in-frame deletion/insertion/insertion-deletion variants as subtypes.

items.item: Conclusion: such variants point to Becker muscular dystrophy rather than Duchenne muscular dystrophy.
items.reason: The quotes explicitly say in-frame mutations are found in Becker patients and allow functional dystrophin, while Duchenne mutations disrupt the reading frame.

items.item: Scope: this is stated as a general association for such DMD variants, not only for a single reported patient or family, and not only as a difference in frequency between patient groups.
items.reason: The quotes state the rule generally and report it across large DMD databases/patient groups, not as a single case or mere group frequency difference.
